chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: Earl Hines's bus accident tour and the Mills Brothers show
summary: On a theater tour from Des Moines to Minneapolis in late 1933, tenor Cecil Irwin was killed; the show included the Mills Brothers, Palmer Brothers and Tip Tap and Toe.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: So, he encouraged me to go. Yeah, Ray and I were -- and Budd Johnson was on that band to. How Budd got in the band was we had an accident and Cecil Irwin was killed -- one of the tenor players in Earl's band. He was killed out right, you know. A grain truck side-swiped us in Iowa. We were going from -- we were playing theaters. We were on a theater tour there. And this was '33, the latter part of '33.

We were going from DesMoines. We just closed a theater in DesMoines. We were going to Minneapolis to open another theater. And we were playing -- but the show -- it was a show. And the Mills Brothers were on the show. And at that -- on that same show was a -- was the Palmer Brothers were singing too with Earl's band. I don't know if you ever heard of them -- singers. Well, they sang with Cab Calloway later. One crippled little boy was with them -- Clarence. And they really sang good, you know. And also Tip, Tap, and
Toe was on that show. Later they called them the Rhythm Kings or something like that. But they were on the show.
